regressions: default and explicit sync/async reads use exactly one identical tenant namespace
both SetAsync overloads replace the same scoped cache entry
background tenant identity shares its own HTTP cache without crossing stores
an awaited real Redis key invalidation reaches a separate web process
tenant clear travels as a qualified prefix and preserves other stores/deployments
a qualified legacy clear remains confined to its named tenant
a clear without server tenant context fails before publication
concurrent HTTP/background accesses retain independent tenant scope

scope: Actual RedisMessageCacheManager/RedisTrackedMemoryCacheBase/RedisMessageBus in three independent web processes. Controlled HTTP store identity and acquired data; no native merchant login, checkout or mobile correlation/FCM consumer acceptance.
